title: Predictive SLO Incident Synthesis Toolkit
author: Aisha Kapoor
summary: A hands-on toolkit and runbook for running predictive SLO simulations that synthesize realistic incident scenarios from SLO drift/error-budget consumption and validate operational tooling, capacity guardrails, and incident review readiness.
body:
## Purpose

This page documents the Predictive SLO Incident Synthesis Toolkit: a reproducible set of simulations and exercises that turn SLO signal drift into realistic incident scenarios. The goal is to evaluate whether our SLOs, error-budget policies, capacity models, observability, and incident-review workflows behave as intended before a real outage. Use this kit for quarterly resilience exercises, pre-release readiness, and postmortem drills.

---

## Scope and audience

- Audience: SREs, service owners, oncall engineers, product reliability leads, and reliability tooling engineers.
- Scope: multi-tenant inference services (model-serving paths), autoscaling behavior, quantized-serving tails, admission controllers, and error-budget enforcement systems.
- Out-of-scope: single-tenant customer upgrade procedures, legal/customer comms templates (see customer-success).

---

## Concepts / assumptions

1. SLO types covered: latency (p50/p95/p99), success rate (>= 200 OK or valid token outputs), and freshness (model artifact/version recency).
2. Error-budget policy: tokenized error budget with tiered reallocation policies and preemptive throttles.
3. Capacity model: heterogeneous GPU pool (A100/RTX-class/FP16-quantized buckets) with warm pools and cold-start penalties.
4. Observability: metrics (latency_quantiles, success_rate, token_count), traces (path, model_variant), and token-level evidence sampling.

---

## Quick reference: key thresholds

| Metric | SLO target | Burn threshold (alert) | Runbook trigger |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| p95 latency (generation, ms) | <= 350ms | 0.5x error budget/day | Initiate mitigation runbook step 2 |
| p99 latency (generation, ms) | <= 900ms | 0.25x error budget/hour | Emergency capacity hedging |
| Success rate (valid response) | >= 99.6% | 0.2% absolute drop | Canary rollback and model-variant fallback |
| Token spend per-minute (tenant group) | N/A (billing) | 2x usual spike | Throttle / tenant-shaping policy |

---

## Toolkit components

1. Simulation harness (python) — input: workload profiles, model variants, failure-injection rules.
2. Telemetry replayer — consumes synthetic metrics/traces and pushes to our observability pipeline (Prometheus remote write / OTLP).
3. Incident synthesizer — maps SLO drift patterns to incident narratives, evidence bundles, and artifact IDs for postmortem practice.
4. Capacity mutator — small controller that simulates node loss, GPU preemption, and cold-starts for warm pools.
4. Playbook runner — sequences human and automated responses (alerts, throttles, canary rollbacks).

---

## Running a standard quarterly simulation (step-by-step)

1. Preparation (2–3 days before exercise)
   - Owner: service steward + SRE exercise coordinator.
   - Select target tenant groups and model routes (primary, fallback) and confirm no active customer migrations.
   - Bump telemetry sandbox write quota: grant temporary write tokens for synthetic streams.
   - Notify leadership and paging rotations (exercise, not real outage).

2. Configure the scenario (4–6 hours)
   - Pick scenario template: choose from [latency-tail, sustained-headroom-loss, tenant-burst, model-regression].
   - Provide parameters: baseline qps, p50/p95/p99 baselines, warm-pool-size, cold-start-latency-ms, percent of model-variants receiving degraded weights.
   - Example CLI to init:
     - python synth/init_scenario.py --template latency-tail --qps 1200 --warm-pool 40 --cold-start 1200

3. Inject capacity perturbations (controlled)
   - Trigger node eviction: ./harness/capacity_mutator --evict 3 --zone eu-west1-b --type A100
   - Simulate increased K/V cache misses (x3) for specific model variants.

4. Start telemetry replay and incident synthesizer (T0)
   - Start telemetry replayer: ./telemetry/replayer --scenario-id SYN-2026-01 --otlp-endpoint https://sandbox-otel.internal
   - Launch incident synthesizer: ./synth/incidentalize --scenario-id SYN-2026-01 --severity medium --notify oncall

5. Observe and enact mitigations (0–90 minutes)
   - Oncall follows standard SLO mitigation runbook: reduce backpressure, apply throttles, increase warm-pool size if autoscaler lag detected.
   - Automated responses should trigger: tenant-shaper engages, model-variant fallback to quantized-safe variant, and canary rollback if success_rate drops >0.5%.

6. Post-sim wrap-up (1–2 days)
   - Collect evidence bundle: telemetry snapshot (metrics, traces), synthesized incident narrative, decision timeline, and automation logs.
   - Run retrospective with stakeholders (SRE, product, runtime team, customer success).

---

## Example scenario templates (short descriptions)

- latency-tail: increase p99 latency on quantized-serving paths by introducing cold-starts and kernel regressions.
- sustained-headroom-loss: gradual capacity erosion across regions due to scheduled maintenance compounding autoscaler inefficiency.
- tenant-burst: a single tenant’s qps increases 20x and consumes shared cache, provoking fairshare throttles.
- model-regression: a newly rolled model variant exhibits higher token generation latency and lower success_rate for a subset of prompts.

---

## Acceptance criteria for runbook/tooling validation

- Alerts fire within deterministic windows: burn alerts within 5 minutes of simulated breach.
- Mitigation automation (throttle/canary rollback) triggers and completes within target RPOs: 10 minutes for automated throttles, 20 minutes for rollback.
- Observability artifacts are complete: traces include model_variant and kv-cache-hit tags 100% of sampled requests.
- Post-sim incident narrative contains required evidence: timeline, hypothesis, mitigation actions with owners, and impact quantification.

---

## Automation checks and example telemetry mapping

- Ensure these tags/labels are present in replayer outputs: service=redwood-runtime, route, tenant_group, model_variant, kv_cache_hit, quantized=true|false.

Example sample mapping table:

| Replay metric name | Target metric | Unit | Prometheus/OTLP metric |
|---|---|---:|---|
| synth.latency.p95 | p95 generation | ms | runtime.request.latency.p95 (histogram) |
| synth.success.rate | success rate | pct | runtime.request.success_rate (gauge) |
| synth.token.count | tokens/min | tokens | billing.tokens.rate |

---

## Post-simulation incident review template (required fields)

1. Title and scenario-id
2. Summary (1 paragraph)
3. Timeline (minute resolution) — include synthetic event IDs and telemetry pointers
4. Root cause hypothesis and evidence mapping (metric -> trace -> change/event)
5. Mitigations attempted (order, automation vs manual) and outcome
6. What worked (observability, runbook steps, automation success)
7. Gaps and action items (owner and ETA)
8. Acceptance criteria verification (pass/fail)

---

## Ownership and cadence

- Exercise owner: reliability-initiatives (rotating steward: Eng-SRE oncall manager).
- Tech owner(s): runtime-team (tooling + capacity_mutator), telemetry-team (replayer pipes), service-steward.
- Cadence: quarterly for platform-critical services, monthly for new model onboarding.

---

## Safety and coordination checklist

- Exercise must run in a sandboxed telemetry tenancy; production scraping hooks must be disabled for exercise IDs.
- Customer-impacting controls: all throttles and tenant-evictions should be applied only to synthetic tenant IDs unless explicit customer opt-in is granted.
- Legal/Compliance: if scenario touches regulated regions, notify security & compliance 48 hours ahead.

---

## Troubleshooting common failures

- Telemetry not ingested: check OTLP token, validate collector config (collector logs at /var/log/otel-collector).
- Autoscaler not reacting: validate admission-controller logs and check warm-pool health endpoint: /internal/warm_pool/health.
- Incident synthesizer fails to attach traces: confirm trace sampling rate >= 10% in replayer flags.

---

## Useful CLI snippets and locations

- Start replayer: ./telemetry/replayer --scenario SYN-2026-01 --otlp https://sandbox-otel.internal --sample-rate 0.12
- Evict nodes: ./capmut/evict --count 2 --pool gpu-a100-eu --reason "simulation"
- Collect evidence bundle: ./evidence/collect --scenario SYN-2026-01 --out ./evidence/SYN-2026-01.bundle.tar.gz

---

## Follow-up and continuous improvement

- After each exercise, update the central SLO contract registry if acceptance criteria reveal mismatches.
- Feed failing scenarios into the CI harness so that model onboarding and runtime changes are validated against a growing library of failure modes.
- Schedule a 90-day remediation verification for all action items with owners.
